claims.claim: Root causes of Shadow-to-Master UPDATE/DELETE drops are: (1) DELETE WHERE _source_id = ? failing with SQLSTATE 42703 on Master tables where _source_id was dropped, coupled with binarySearchSplit discarding the entire single-task NATS batch; (2) Split-Brain _gpay_id between RunEvents (SHA-256) and Run (Sonyflake) breaking Segment B Recon/Heal; (3) Incremental Run() filtering only _gpay_id > lastGpayID which misses updated rows whose _gpay_id did not change; and (4) BatchBuffer grouping by signature before cross-signature deduplication.

The proposed solution in 09_tasks_solution_shadow_master_update_drop.md resolves all root causes by: looking up Shadow _gpay_id in RunEvents and allowing _gpay_id updates when conflictTarget != "_gpay_id", deleting on Master via conflictTarget/_gpay_id instead of _source_id, splitting single-task Events/SourceIDs payloads in binarySearchSplit, deduplicating by PrimaryKeyValue before signature grouping in BatchBuffer, and scanning recently updated Shadow rows / triggering NATS transmute after ReconHealer.

The proposed changes are localized to TransmuterModule (transmuter.go), TransmuteHandler (transmute_handler.go), BatchBuffer (batch_buffer.go / batch_buffer_utils.go), and ReconHealer / ReconExecuteHealHandler without altering external NATS subject contracts or requiring destructive DDL migrations on Master tables.
The proposed solution adheres strictly to the existing codebase architecture and patterns, reusing deterministicGpayID, isRetryableDBError, quoteTransmuteIdent, and GORM batch queries on Shadow DB.
